'''Vipin Kumar Tripathi''' (alternately known as '''VK Tripathi'''; born 11 March 1948) is an [[Indian people|Indian]] [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] physicist, activist, and a  professor emeritus at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Delhi]] (IIT Delhi).  Known for his contributions to plasma physics, particularly in microwave-plasma interactions and laser-plasma studies, Tripathi has also gained recognition for his [[social activism]] through the Sadbhav Mission, which promotes communal harmony and education in India.

==Early life and education ==
Vipin Kumar Tripathi was born on 11 March 1948 to [[Indian freedom fighter]] and wrestler Hardas Sharma in Piprai, [[Jhansi]], [[Uttar Pradesh, India]]. Raised in a multicultural environment, he was influenced by his father's [[Muslims|Muslim]] mentor Ahmed Baksh, whom he credits for his upbringing, fostering his commitment to social harmony.<ref name="telegraphindia" /><ref name="tnn" />

He earned his [[Master of Science|M. S. degree]] in Physics from [[Agra University]] in 1967 and completed his [[Ph.D.]] in Physics at IIT Delhi in 1971.<ref name="tnn">{{cite news |author1=Shradha Chettri |date=22 October 2019 |title=Delhi: Meet the 71-year-old pamphlet man with a message of peace |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/meet-the-71-year-old-pamphlet-man-with-a-message-of-peace/articleshow/71696237.cms |access-date=16 January 2020 |publisher=Times of India |language=English}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Professor VK Tripathi: I was born a Hindu, raised by a Muslim |url=https://www.awazthevoice.in/personality-news/professor-vk-tripathi-i-am-born-a-hindu-but-i-was-raised-a-muslim-19155.html |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=www.awazthevoice.in |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-16 |title=Septuagenarian Indian activist marks Independence Day with fast for Gaza |url=https://arab.news/jmv4p |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=Arab News |language=en}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Tripathi began his academic career as a lecturer at IIT Delhi in 1970, focusing on the nonlinear interaction of [[electromagnetic waves]] with plasmas.

In 1976, he joined the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] and later as a [[research associate]], working on [[radio frequency heating]] of fusion plasmas.

Returning to IIT Delhi in 1983, he served as a Professor of Physics for nearly three decades, retiring as Professor Emeritus. During his tenure, he established the Plasma Group at IIT Delhi, which conducted pioneering research on [[gyrotron]]s, [[free-electron laser]]s, laser-plasma interactions, and material processing.<ref name="tnn" /><ref name="profile">{{cite web |title=Profile of Vipin Kumar Tripathi |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37320273400 |website=[[IEEE]] |access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref><ref name="telegraphindia">{{Cite web|title=Professor fights for Kashmir, armed with pamphlets|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/professor-fights-for-kashmir-armed-with-pamphlets/cid/1706570|website=Telegraph India|author1=Pheroze L. Vincent|access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref>

His research contributions include studies on parametric instabilities in laser-produced plasmas, [[thermonuclear fusion]], plasma-aided radiation guiding, and Cherenkov terahertz generation.

Notable publications include works on [[stimulated Brillouin scattering]], [[plasmonics]], and high-power laser-plasma interactions. Tripathi’s Plasma Lab at IIT Delhi, initiated in 1980, developed innovative plasma sources like the Compact ECR Plasma Source (CEPS) and Large Volume Plasma System (LVPS), with applications in semiconductor processing, ion implantation, and waste mitigation. His team also designed high-power microwave components, including coaxial triple stub tuners and low-cost power supplies for plasma applications.

== Activism ==
In 1990, he formed a Forum for Secular Indians in [[United States]] which was later named as 'Sadbhav Mission' in response to the [[Bhagalpur riots]], aiming to foster grassroots resistance against communalism and promote education.<ref name="sadbhav">{{cite web |title=About Sadbhav Mission |url=http://www.sadbhavmission.org/about.html |website=Sadbhav Mission |access-date=8 February 2020 |archive-date=15 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215121501/http://www.sadbhavmission.org/about.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Vats |first=Nischai |date=2019-12-27 |title=A Gandhian in our midst |url=https://thepatriot.in/reports/a-gandhian-in-our-midst-14283 |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=The Patriot |language=en-US}}</ref>

Tripathi left the USA saddened by the [[1982 Lebanon War]], when [[Israel]] attacked [[Lebanon]] and around 20,000 people were killed and the US supported Israel.<ref name=":2" /><ref name="telegraphindia" />

In 1990, when [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] started its 'Rath Yatra' with [[Lal Krishna Advani]] as the star performer, Tripathi introduced his 'Aatm Manthan Yatra' from [[Raj Ghat and associated memorials|Rajghat]] wherein he along with some volunteers and other supporters distributed around 4,000 flyers across Delhi.<ref name=":2" />

His activism, often conducted single-handedly on the streets of [[Delhi]], has been noted for its dedication to social justice, with Tripathi earning descriptions as a “pamphlet man with a message of peace.” In 2025, he distributed fliers highlighting [[Gaza Strip famine|mass starvation in Gaza]], emphasising universal human compassion.<ref name="national">{{cite web |date=16 December 2019 |title=Retired IIT Professor's solitary campaign against the National Register of Citizens: Listen to VK Tripathi |url=https://www.nationalheraldindia.com/india/retired-iit-professors-solitary-campaign-against-the-national-register-of-citizens-listen-to-vk-tripathi |access-date=8 February 2020 |website=National Herald India}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=17 August 2025 |title=77-year-old ex-IIT professor stopped at Rajghat fast for Gaza; daughter alleges police hostility |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/77-year-old-ex-iit-professor-stopped-at-rajghat-fast-for-gaza-daughter-alleges-police-hostility/cid/2118381 |work=[[The Telegraph (India)]]}}</ref>

Through the Sadbhav Mission, he has written and distributed pamphlets on issues like the [[Article 370 of the Constitution of India|Abrogation of Article 370]] and [[Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019|CAA]] as a mode of protest.<ref name="edu">{{cite web |author1=Pawanjot Kaur and Sunil Rawat |date=14 October 2019 |title=To Educate People on Kashmir, a 71-Year-Old Has Taken to the Streets All Alone |url=https://thewire.in/rights/watch-to-educate-people-on-kashmir-a-71-year-old-has-taken-to-the-streets-all-alone |access-date=16 January 2020 |website=The Wire}}</ref><ref name="national" />

In 2025, VK Tripathi went on a hunger fast at [[Raj Ghat and associated memorials|Rajghat]] and distributed pamphlets related to [[Gaza war]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Avdhesh |date=2025-08-26 |title=A day in the life of an ex-IIT professor crusading for Gaza, against hate in Delhi |url=https://www.newslaundry.com/2025/08/26/a-day-in-the-life-of-an-ex-iit-professor-crusading-for-gaza-against-hate-in-delhi |access-date=2025-08-31 |website=Newslaundry |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=77-year-old ex-IIT professor stopped at Rajghat fast for Gaza; daughter alleges police hostility |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/77-year-old-ex-iit-professor-stopped-at-rajghat-fast-for-gaza-daughter-alleges-police-hostility/cid/2118381 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250823135751/https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/77-year-old-ex-iit-professor-stopped-at-rajghat-fast-for-gaza-daughter-alleges-police-hostility/cid/2118381 |archive-date=23 August 2025 |access-date=2025-08-31 |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Tripathi has received several accolades for his academic and social contributions:

•  '''[[Fellow]], [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA)''': Recognized for his contributions to plasma physics.

•  '''Fellow, [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] (NASI)''': Honored for his scientific achievements.

•  '''JC Bose Memorial Award, Indian Physics Association''': Acknowledged for his research in plasma physics.

•  '''[[Honorary Professor]], [[Banaras Hindu University]]''': For his contributions to physics education and research.

== Personal life ==
Tripathi is married and has two sons and a daughter, Rakhi Tripathi, who has publicly supported his activism efforts. He resides in [[Sarvodaya Enclave]], Delhi and remains active in both academic and social spheres.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

==Selected publications==
Tripathi's publications include:<ref name="profile" /><ref name="research">{{cite web |title=V.K. Tripathi's research works |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/2093627662_VK_Tripathi |website=ResearchGate |access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref>
*Parametric instabilities in laser produced plasmas. 
* ''Thermonuclear fusion''
* ''Plasma-aided radiation guiding in a free-electron laser''
* ''Stimulated Brillouin scattering of a laser beam in a plasma channel''
* ''Cherenkov Terahertz Generation by Electron Bunches in a Dielectric Lined Resonator''
*''Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Verification of the Permeability Measurements of Thick Films at Microwave Frequencies''
*''Laser wakefield bubble regime acceleration of electrons in a preformed non uniform plasma channel''
* ''Plasmonics''
* ''High power laser plasma interaction''
* ''Fundamentals of plasma physics''
